questions.question: A wooden piece in the shape of a cuboid is divided into five equal parts by cutting it with four cuts perpendicular to its length, and it turns out that each piece is a cube of volume 27 cm³. What is the total surface area (in cm²) of the cuboid?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Volume of each cube = 27 cm3

**Concept used:**

Volume of cube = a³

Total surface area of a cuboid = 2(l × b + b × h + l × h)

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50c4d7f25d09d990719ff29e43bc60cc1fcb6a2a6fd59744d619ff8cb4364209.png] 

Side of each cube (a) = 3

So, length of the cuboid = 5 × 3 = 15 cm

Height and breadth of the cuboid = 3 cm

Total surface area of the cuboid = 2(15 × 3 + 3 × 3 + 15 × 3)

⇒ 2 × 99 = 198 cm²

**∴ Total surface area of the cuboid is 198 cm2**

questions.question: The difference between a positive number and its reciprocal increases by a factor of frac{{175}}{{144}} when the number is made to increase by 20%. What is the number?

(x - 1/x) × 175/144 = 6x/5 - 5/6x

⇒ (175x² - 175)/144x = (36x² - 25)30x

⇒ 5(175x2 - 175) = 24(36x2 - 25)

⇒ 875x2 - 875 = 864x2 - 600

⇒ 11x2 = 275

⇒ x2 = 25

**∴ Required number is 5**

questions.question: How many numbers between 500 and 900, both inclusive, are exactly divisible by all the numbers, 12, 15, 20 and 30?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

LCM of 12, 15, 20, 30 = 60

Total number which are divisible by 60 from 1 to 900 = 900/60 = 15

Total number which are divisible by 60 from 1 to 500 = 500/60 = 8

So, between 500 and 900 only 7 numbers are divisible by all the numbers

**∴ Required answer is 7**

**Note: **In the Question it is mentioned that both the numbers are inclusive, i.e. both 500 and 900 are also taken into consideration here.

2 × (24 × 15 × 12) = (36 × 10 × D₂)

questions.question: The material of a sphere of radius r is melted and recast into a hollow cylindrical shell of thickness a and outer radius b. What is its length assuming that no material is lost in recasting?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Outer radius = b

Thickness = a

Radius of sphere = r

**Concept used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3)πr³

Volume of a hollow cylinder= π(R² - r²)h

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

4/3πr³ = π[b² - (b - a)²]h

⇒ 4/3πr3 = π[b2 - b2 - a2 + 2ab]h

⇒ 4/3r3 = [2ab - a2]h

⇒ h = 4r³/3a[2b - a]

**∴ Required length is frac{{4{r³}}}{{3a(2b - a)}}**

questions.question: A lady walks to her office every day from home and maintains a fixed time for the same. On one day she decreases her speed by 25%. By what fraction of her usual time will she be late on that day?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Time = D/S

**Calculation:**

Let her speed be 4x

So, on that day her speed was = 3x

Time difference = D/3x - D/4x

⇒ (4D - 3D)/12x = D/12x

Fraction time difference = (D/12x)/(D/4x)

⇒ D/12x × 4x/D = 1/3

**∴ She will be late on that day by 1/3 of her usal time **

questions.question: Two similar pieces of an item were purchased by paying the same amount for each, and they were sold, respectively, for a profit of 25% and a loss of 20%. What was his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

SP = CP + CP × Profit%

SP = CP - Loss × Profit%

**Calculation:**

Let price of each be 100x

So, SP of 1st = 125x

and 2nd = 80x

So total SP = 205x

Total CP = 200x

Profit = 205x - 200x = 5x

Profit % = (5x/200x) × 100

⇒ 2.5%

**∴ Required profit percentage is 2.5**

and Z's share = 100x + 1000

⇒ 340x = 119000

Now, Amount of profit shared = 120000 × 1/5 × 9/10 = 21600

So, Share of X = 21600 × 35/120 = Rs. 6300

**∴ The share (in ₹) of X out of it is 6300**

questions.question: The line graph that can replace a histogram is called a/an:

options.text: cumulative frequency less than type graph
cumulative frequency more than type graph

questions.solution:
The line graph that can replace a histogram is called a __**frequency polygon.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Frequency Polygon:** A frequency polygon is a graph constructed by using lines to join the midpoints of each interval or bin. The heights of the points represent the frequencies. A frequency polygon can be created from the histogram or by calculating the midpoints of the bins from the frequency distribution table.

questions.question: A certain sum was invested for three years in a scheme in which the interest gets compounded annually. During the first two years, the scheme provided growths at the rates of 80% and 60%, respectively, but during the third year there was a decline by 40%. What was the overall interest rate for three years?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Successive increase = x + x + x²/100

**Calculation:**

Let principal be Rs. 125x

So,

After 3 years amount = 125x × 9/5 × 8/5 × 3/5

⇒ 216x

So, Intereset = 216x - 125x = 91

Cumulative rate of interest = 91/125 × 100 = 72.8%

Now,

We know the concept of successive increase of rate

From option,

20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = 44

Again 44 + 20 + (44 × 20)/100 = 72.8%

**∴ Required rate of interest is 20.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] __Confusion Points__**The effective interest rate for three years is 72.8%.

The overall interest rate will be 20%.

It is so because the effective interest rate of 20% for three years is 72.8%.

Let's understand:

20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = 44

Again 44 + 20 + (44 × 20)/100 = 72.8%

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally; the distance between their centres is 12 cm and the sum of their areas (in cm²) is 74 π. What is the radius of the smaller circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given, R + r = 12 and R² + r² = 74

We need to guess two numbers whose sum is 12 and the sum of their squares is 74.

Let's check 7 and 5: 7 + 5 = 12 and 7² + 5² = 49 + 25 = 74.

Both conditions are satisfied.

Hence, the radius of the smaller circle is 5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two circles touch externally, so the distance between their centres is R + r = 12 cm.

Sum of their areas = πR² + πr² = 74π cm²

**Formula Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = (a + b)² − 4ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ π(R² + r²) = 74π

⇒ R² + r² = 74

We know that (R + r)² = R² + r² + 2Rr

⇒ 12² = 74 + 2Rr

⇒ 144 − 74 = 2Rr

⇒ 70 = 2Rr ⇒ Rr = 35

Now, finding the value of (R − r):

⇒ (R − r)² = (R + r)² − 4Rr

⇒ (R − r)² = 144 − 4 × 35

⇒ (R − r)² = 144 − 140 = 4

⇒ R − r = 2

Solving R + r = 12 and R − r = 2:

⇒ 2R = 14 ⇒ R = 7 cm

⇒ 2r = 10 ⇒ r = 5 cm

The radius of the smaller circle is 5 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circles Touching Externally

When two circles touch externally, the distance between their centres is equal to the sum of their radii (R + r). The number of common tangents they can have is exactly 3.

Circles Touching Internally

When two circles touch internally, the distance between their centres is equal to the difference of their radii (|R − r|). The number of common tangents they can have is exactly 1.

Length of Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length of the Direct Common Tangent can be calculated using the formula: √(d² − (R − r)²), where d is the distance between their centres.

questions.question: The average daily expenditure of a person during the month of February 2020 was ₹ 120. The average expenditure for the first 15 days was ₹ 142, and for the last 15 days was ₹ 96. What was his expenditure (in ₹) on 15th February?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average daily expenditure of a person during the month of February 2020 was ₹ 120

The average expenditure for the first 15 days was ₹ 142, and for the last 15 days was ₹ 96

**Concept used:**

Average = Sum of elements/No. of elements

**Calculation:**

Total expenditure of 1st 15 days = 15 × 142 = 2130

Total expenditure of last 15 days = 15 × 96 = 1440

Total = 2130 + 1440 = 3570

Total expenditure of the month = 120 × 29 = 3480

So, Expenditure of the 15th day = 3570 - 3480 = 90

**∴ Required answer is 90**

questions.question: An article was subject to three successive discounts, whereby a customer had to pay ₹ 2,366.8 less than the marked price of ₹ 12,500. If the rates of the first two discounts were, respectively, 12% and 6%, then what was the rate percentage of the third discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Final Selling Price (SP) = 12500 − 2366.8 = 10133.2

Using successive multiplying factors: 12500 × 0.88 × 0.94 × (1 − d/100) = 10133.2

⇒ 10340 × (1 − d/100) = 10133.2

Third discount value = 10340 − 10133.2 = 206.8

Third discount % = (206.8 ÷ 10340) × 100 = 2%

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹12,500

Total discount = ₹2,366.8

First discount (d₁) = 12%

Second discount (d₂) = 6%

Let the third discount be d₃%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Total Discount

⇒ SP = 12500 − 2366.8 = 10133.2

⇒ Price after 1st discount = 12500 × (100 − 12) ÷ 100 = 12500 × 0.88 = 11000

⇒ Price after 2nd discount = 11000 × (100 − 6) ÷ 100 = 11000 × 0.94 = 10340

⇒ Price after 3rd discount = 10340 × (100 − d₃) ÷ 100 = 10133.2

⇒ 10340 − 103.4d₃ = 10133.2

⇒ 103.4d₃ = 10340 − 10133.2 = 206.8

⇒ d₃ = 206.8 ÷ 103.4 = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two or more discounts are applied sequentially on the Marked Price, they are called successive discounts. The formula for effective discount of two successive discounts d₁ and d₂ is: D = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Selling Price Formula

For a sequence of three discounts d₁%, d₂%, and d₃%, the Final Selling Price is given by: SP = MP × (1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100) × (1 − d₃/100).

Marked Price (MP) vs Selling Price (SP)

Marked Price is the listed price of the article. Selling Price is the price at which it is actually sold after applying all discounts. Discount = MP − SP.

questions.question: Two clocks were synchronised at 11 a.m. on a Sunday. Thereafter, every day they were, respectively, found to gain and lose one minute per day. What time, expressed in hours and minutes, will the second clock show when the first clock shows 10 p.m. on the next Friday?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two clocks were synchronised at 11 a.m. on a Sunday.

Every day they were, respectively, found to gain and lose one minute per day.

**Calculation:**

From Sunday 11 a.m to Friday 10 p.m total time = 131 hours

According to the question,

In the case of 1st clock

To go 24(1)/({60)} or (1441/60) hours it is taking 24 hours

So, to go 131 hours it is taking (24 × 131)/(1441/60)

In the case of 2nd clock

In 24 hours it is going (24 - (1)/({60)}) hours or (1439/60) hours

So,

In (24 × 131)/(1441/60) hours it is going [1439/60 × (24 × 131)/(1441/60)]/24

⇒ 1439/11

⇒ 130(9)/({11)}hours

So, from Sunday 11 am + 130(9)/({11)}hours = Friday 9(9)/({11)} p.m or 9 hours 49(1)/({11)} minutes p.m.

**∴ Required answer is 9 hours 49(1)/({11)} minutes p.m.**
